Resilient

/rih-ZIL-yunt/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulties, misfortune, or damage.

Bamboo is remarkably resilient; typhoon winds bend the stalks nearly to the ground, yet they straighten again as soon as the storm passes.

Worked Example

Classmates admired Theo's resilient attitude. A lost chess match or a rejected art-contest entry never discouraged him for more than a day before he was back to practicing and planning his next attempt.

The setbacks still happen and still sting, but Theo has a built-in capacity to bounce back from them quickly. That standing ability to spring back after difficulty, rather than any single recovery, is what makes someone resilient.

How Resilient Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

hardy

hardy: tough enough to survive harsh conditions

buoyant

buoyant: able to bounce back cheerfully

tough

tough: strong under strain

Antonyms

fragile

fragile: easily broken or harmed

brittle

brittle: hard but snapping under stress

How Strong Is It? — flexible → resilient → unbreakable

flexible vs. resilient

flexible vs. resilient: Something flexible bends without complaint, while something resilient goes further and springs back to its original form after being bent or damaged.

unbreakable vs. resilient

unbreakable vs. resilient: Something resilient recovers from damage, while something unbreakable claims it cannot be damaged in the first place.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back

Root — sili

Root — sili: to jump, to leap (Latin salire)

Suffix — -ent

Suffix — -ent: having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Someone or something resilient literally has the quality of leaping back. Pressed down by trouble or damage, it springs back to its original shape or spirit.

Use the root in a new word: assail

Use the root in a new word: assail: Reporters assailed the senator with questions the moment the vote ended, leaping at him from every side.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday

Used of people, materials, and systems alike, as in resilient kids, resilient rubber, and a resilient economy. It names the built-in capacity to bounce back after being affected; resistant, by contrast, describes something that avoids being affected in the first place.
